newsitem.title: USA: Congressmen hold Boston tax party.
newsitem.headline: Congressmen hold Boston tax party.

text.p: Five Republican congressmen held a Boston tax party Tuesday, dumping the U.S. tax code into the Boston harbour from the deck of an 18th century-style ship.

Reps. Dan Schaefer of Colorado and Billy Tauzin of Louisiana, co-sponsors of a bill to abolish the federal income tax, tossed a black cooler filled with U.S. tax code books into the harbour to the cheers of three colleagues and about 40 onlookers.

Reps. Charlie Norwood of Georgia, Michael Crapo of Idaho and Ron Packard of California also took a turn at throwing the cooler, labeled "tea," into the water from the deck of the "Beaver II," an inexact replica of the original Boston Tea Party ship.

Tauzin said his proposal to scrap income taxes with a 15 percent federal retail sales tax would be a fair plan which would "yield the amount of revenue without the income tax code, without all the forms, and most importantly, without April 15."
"April 15 will become just another beautiful spring day in our lives, instead of this day we hate so much, the day the tax man cometh," he told supporters.
